recognize_zh: 甲苯胺藍（Toluidine blue）染色下，多數細胞含粗大、深紫紅色的異染性（metachromasia）顆粒，對比淡藍色細胞質與細胞核；另見少數無顆粒、較大的淡藍色細胞，符合母細胞與嗜鹼性球混合的 CSF 抹片。
features: Cytospin preparation stained with toluidine blue showing numerous cells with coarse metachromatic granules staining deep purple to magenta
Granules often obscure the nucleus and cluster around it, typical of basophils (and possibly mast-cell–differentiated cells)
Admixed larger cells with pale blue, agranular or sparsely granulated cytoplasm and round nuclei, consistent with blasts
Some cells show only a few metachromatic granules in otherwise immature-appearing cytoplasm (partially granulated blasts)
Clean background with scattered extruded granules
describe_en: Toluidine blue–stained CSF cytospin shows a cellular specimen containing numerous cells with coarse metachromatic purple-magenta granules, consistent with basophils, many of which obscure nuclear detail. Interspersed are larger cells with pale blue, largely agranular cytoplasm and round nuclei, some containing sparse metachromatic granules, in keeping with blasts showing basophilic differentiation. Together with the clinical history of CML, the findings are consistent with CNS involvement by myeloid blast phase with prominent basophilia.

ddx.vs: Mast cells are also toluidine blue metachromatic but are larger, round-to-spindle with a central non-lobed nucleus and evenly packed granules, and are tryptase/CD117 bright with CD25; basophils are smaller, lobulated and CD123+/HLA-DR−, requiring flow or IHC to separate.
Eosinophil granules are not metachromatic with toluidine blue (they stain orange-red on Romanowsky stains) and eosinophils are typically bilobed.
APL granules are azurophilic and MPO-strong but not metachromatic, and Auer rod bundles rather than toluidine blue positivity are characteristic.
